content:
Got a chance to meet the OG Chinmaya Amte in Gurgaon!

And, as you can imagine, we had plenty to talk about. From LinkedIn comments to AI, socio-political debates and even the economics of splitting a bill.. 😂

𝐈𝐭’𝐬 𝐟𝐮𝐧𝐧𝐲 𝐡𝐨𝐰 𝐋𝐢𝐧𝐤𝐞𝐝𝐈𝐧 𝐰𝐨𝐫𝐤𝐬. You start noticing someone in comments section of posts, appreciate their takes, occasionally come across their content and eventually end up having some pretty interesting conversations offline.

That’s how I first came across Chinmaya and tbh.. catching up with him was a lot of fun!

We spoke about his journey to becoming an OG creator, how AI is changing the way we think and create (from being a refiner of thoughts to… a definer of thoughts?) and got into some interesting socio-political discussions too.

Now, those socio-political discussions are staying between us. You never know who's watching on LinkedIn 😂

One thing I really appreciate about Chinmaya is his very 𝙈𝙪𝙢𝙗𝙖𝙞𝙠𝙖𝙧 way of looking at things.

Take TTMM, for instance. 𝙏𝙪 𝙏𝙚𝙧𝙖, 𝙈𝙖𝙞 𝙈𝙚𝙧𝙖. Everyone pays for their own share.
No confusion, no awkward calculations, no keeping track of who owes whom.

Honestly, how cool is that? Mumbai has a way of making even splitting a bill sound iconic.

And then came our final photo session. We decided to take some “𝐩𝐥𝐚𝐧𝐧𝐞𝐝 𝐜𝐚𝐧𝐝𝐢𝐝” pictures, which is probably the biggest contradiction in photography.

Naturally, they didn’t turn out as planned. So here we are, posting a good old normal picture instead 😎

All in all, a memorable evening, some great conversations and a reminder that LinkedIn connections can go well beyond the comments section.

Great catching up, Chinmaya!

𝐏.𝐒. I might just start using TTMM more often. Though I suspect my friends wont be too impressed.

#linkedin #meetup #chinmaya
comment: TTMM works because it removes the invisible ledger that often builds up in friendships. The same principle applies to teams: clear expectations upfront prevent awkward conversations later.
